wins.text: Q1 total revenue was a record $14.9B, up 25% YoY; adjusted EBITDA was a record $10.1B (68% of revenue), up 41% YoY — both above guidance of 66%
AI revenue of $4.1B in Q1, up 77% YoY, beating prior guidance of $3.8B on stronger-than-expected networking shipments to hyperscalers
Infrastructure software gross margin expanded to 92.5% from 88% a year ago; operating margin improved to 76% from 59% YoY, reflecting disciplined VMware integration
~70% of the largest 10,000 VMware customers have adopted VCF full-stack subscription, up from a largely perpetual-license base; over 60% conversion to subscription complete
4 additional hyperscalers now deeply engaged with Broadcom to develop custom AI accelerators (XPUs), expanding the pipeline beyond the 3 existing volume customers

risks.text: Non-AI semiconductor revenue of $4.1B was down 9% sequentially on seasonal wireless decline; enterprise networking remains flattish in H1 FY25 as customers work through channel inventory; industrial resales down double digits in Q1 and expected down again in Q2

Free cash flow of $6B represented only 40% of revenue, pressured by ~$68.8B gross debt (VMware acquisition), high cash interest expense, and elevated cash taxes from Section 174 delay and corporate AMT
Tariff uncertainty on semiconductors flagged as unresolved; Hock noted it is 'too early to know where we all land' and suggested clarity may be 3–6 months away

AI diffusion / export control rules expected in May raised by analysts; while Hock said 'no concerns,' he declined to confirm whether any XPU customers are outside the U.S., adding a layer of geopolitical opacity
Q1 networking mix was an unusually high ~40% of AI revenue vs. a normalized ~30%; management flagged this as a 'temporary blip,' implying potential sequential mix headwind in coming quarters

guidance_items.detail: Q2 consolidated revenue guided to ~$14.9B, up 19% YoY — in line with Q1 actuals, implying flat sequential growth
Q2 AI revenue guided to $4.4B, up 44% YoY, above Q1's $4.1B; total semiconductor revenue guided to ~$8.4B, up 17% YoY
Q2 infrastructure software revenue guided to ~$6.5B, up 23% YoY (slight sequential step-down from Q1's $6.7B due to Q4 deal slip-ins)
Q2 adjusted EBITDA guided to ~66% of revenue vs. Q1's 68%, reflecting higher R&D investment in leading-edge AI and ~20 bps sequential gross margin compression from revenue mix
Non-GAAP tax rate for Q2 and full FY2025 expected at ~14%

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Impact of AI diffusion / export control rules (expected May) on existing XPU customer shipments and whether any customers are in China
Conversion risk from XPU design engagements to actual volume deployment — concern that design wins may not translate to promised volumes
Potential M&A activity, specifically around Intel product assets
